images.title: Two torans, same length
images.purpose: Show that 4 strips of 6 cm and 3 strips of 8 cm make torans of the same length, 24 cm.
images.composition: Two horizontal torans stacked one above the other in the centre, left ends aligned, with a single dashed line marking where both end; plenty of white space above and below.
exact_structure: Upper toran, name Anshu to its left: exactly 4 teal #0072B2 rectangular cloth strips of equal length placed end to end, each strip with the text 6 cm inside it and one small teal triangular pennant hanging below it.

Lower toran, name Guna to its left: exactly 3 amber #E69F00 rectangular cloth strips of equal length placed end to end, each strip with the text 8 cm inside it and one small amber triangular pennant hanging below it.
Strip lengths are drawn to scale: each amber strip is 4/3 times as long as each teal strip, so both torans have exactly the same total length.
Both torans start at the same left edge; one vertical dashed reddish purple #CC79A7 line touches the right ends of both torans.
The text 24 cm sits at the bottom of the dashed line.
rejection: other than exactly 4 teal strips and 3 amber strips
the two torans ending at different places, or strips not drawn to the 6 to 8 scale
a total length other than 24 cm
images.takeaway: A length both torans can reach is a multiple of 6 and of 8, and 24 cm is the first one.
images.description: Anshu's toran of four 6 cm strips and Guna's toran of three 8 cm strips both end at the same dashed line marked 24 cm.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on toran lengths from strips of 6 cm and 8 cm.
images.teaching_notes: Count the strips in each toran and multiply, 4 × 6 and 3 × 8, to see why both reach 24 cm.

image_decisions.why: Two torans of equal length make the idea of a common multiple concrete.
